newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold closes closes slighly down.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold closes closes slighly down.

text.p: Hong Kong's bullion market eased Tuesday with traders reporting little activity aside from a small amount of Japanese gold selling.
"It's very quiet apart from some Japanse selling," commented a trader at a local bank. "The Japanese are selling only small amounts, but we don't know how much overall they will be selling."
A European bank dealer said the Japanese sales were triggered by a higher dollar-yen exchange rate and did not have much effect on the Hong Kong market.
Traders cited a lack of local and international influences for the slow market, which opened at US$381.50/382.00, the day's high, and slowly slipped to close at US$381.00/381.50, the day's low.
Local gold closed at HK$3,512 a tael, HK$1 down from Monday's close of HK$3,513.

An announcement Monday by Belgian National Bank Governor Alfons Verplaetse that there would be no more Belgian central bank gold sales failed to move the Hong Kong market. He said G-10 central bankers had an agreement not to destabllize the gold market by large sales.
Local traders said the Belgian announcement firmed markets in London and New York Monday but had no noticable effect in Hong Kong.
"There has been no reaction on our end," said one local dealer.
